title: Numerical Sanity Check Judge
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Judgment activity in which learners give each of eight illustrative reported results one of five verdicts: Plausible, Exceeds a limit, Disagrees with a hand calculation, Violates scaling, or Impossible value. Each result gets one attempt in a fixed order; the sim then reveals the correct verdict, the reason, and the quick calculation that exposes the problem. The run ends with a score out of 8 and whether the mastery threshold of 7 was met.

educational.topic: Numerical sanity checks for AI-written research code
learningObjectives: Judge each of eight reported results as plausible or as violating one of four kinds of sanity check, with at least 7 of 8 judged correctly
prerequisites: Numerical sanity check and its four failing kinds: exceeds a limit, disagrees with a hand calculation, violates scaling, impossible value
The RC low-pass cutoff f_c = 1 / (2 pi R C)

canvasDimensions.controlHeight: rows x 35 + 10 (80 to 150, depending on width)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons and a checkbox reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; the chosen verdict is marked with a filled circle and aria-pressed; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or cross symbols as well as a blue or orange border; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Plausible / Exceeds a limit / Disagrees with a hand calculation / Violates scaling / Impossible value
controls.purpose: Five verdict buttons. Choose one verdict for the current result; the choice can be changed until it is submitted. Disabled after submission.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen verdict as the single attempt for the current result and shows the feedback.

controls.label: Next / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after a verdict is submitted. Advances to the next result, and after result 8 shows the score.

controls.label: Show the checks
controls.purpose: Shows a one-line hint about each verdict. Exploration only; it does not affect the score.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Single-attempt judgment items with immediate explanatory feedback and a revealed quick calculation
keyQuestions: Is this result plausible, and if not, which check does it fail?
What limit, hand calculation, or scaling law must this result obey?
commonMisconceptions: A result printed to many digits is precise and therefore right
A result that is merely different from expectation is an error
A simulation result can be trusted because the simulator is well known
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 verdicts correct on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Learner writes the quick calculation for each result before submitting
